content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted. **This is the first SDD gate — please review it before we plan or write any code.**

## 📄 Spec ready for review

- **Feature directory:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/`
- **Spec file:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Quality checklist:** all items pass (`checklists/requirements.md`)

### What the spec proposes — a bookmark manager, built in priority slices

| Priority | User story | In short |
|----------|-----------|----------|
| **P1** | Save a bookmark | Enter an address (+ optional title), it's validated and saved |
| **P1** | Browse & open | See your list, click to open the original page |
| **P2** | Edit & delete | Fix or remove bookmarks, with a delete confirmation |
| **P3** | Find & organize | Search by keyword, tag bookmarks, filter by tag |

It also covers edge cases (duplicate links, missing `http://`, very long titles, big collections) and sets measurable success criteria (e.g. save your first bookmark in under 30 seconds, no data loss across reloads, responsive with 500+ bookmarks).

### ⚠️ Key assumptions I made — please confirm

Rather than block on questions, I chose reasonable defaults and documented them. The important ones:

1. **Single user, personal use** — no accounts, sign-in, or sharing. *This is the biggest scope call.* If you meant a multi-user or shared product, tell me now — it changes a lot.
2. **Web app** in the browser — no native mobile/desktop app or browser extension in v1.
3. **Local persistence** — bookmarks survive reload on the same device; no cross-device sync in v1.
4. **Manual entry** — no auto-import from a browser and no automatic page-title/thumbnail fetching in v1.
5. **http/https links only.**

### 👉 Your move at this gate

- **Looks good?** Say so and I'll proceed to `speckit-plan` (the implementation plan) — still no code until you approve that too.
- **Want changes?** Tell me what's wrong or missing and I'll revise the spec.
- **Want me to probe ambiguities first?** I can run `speckit-clarify` for structured questions before planning.

I'll wait for your confirmation before moving on.

The single-user browser app and same-device storage are fine, as is limiting links to normal web addresses. But the proposed scope is missing important parts of what I mean by managing bookmarks, so please revise it before planning.

When I save a link, I expect the app to collect its title, description, favicon, and preview image automatically, while letting me edit the title and description. Saving an address that already exists should take me to the existing bookmark for editing, not allow a duplicate.

Each bookmark should also support a note, multiple tags, an unread/read-later state, and archiving. The normal list should clearly show the title, description, tags, and favicon. Archived links should be hidden from normal browsing and search, with separate unread and archived views.

Search needs to cover the title, description, note, and address without caring about capitalization. I also want `#tag` searches, exact phrases, and combinations using AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses. Please include sorting, tag suggestions from tags I already use, selecting several bookmarks for bulk changes, and applying an action to everything matching the current view.

I’d also like saved reusable searches, page snapshots—including keeping PDFs as PDFs—Internet Archive saving, bookmark import/export, and basic display preferences such as sorting, number of items shown, and font size.

Finally, importing browser bookmarks should not be ruled out: Netscape-style bookmark-file import and export should be included. Please update the specification and bring it back for review.

The implementation plan and its design artifacts are ready. **This is the plan-review gate — please review before I generate tasks or write any code.**

## 📐 Plan ready — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md`

**Artifacts:** `plan.md`, `research.md` (12 decisions), `data-model.md`, `contracts/` (api, search-grammar, netscape-format), `quickstart.md`. Constitution file is an unfilled template, so there are no ratified project gates; I held the plan to the method's baseline (spec-first, simplicity, testability) — it passes with no complexity to justify.

### The core architectural decision — why there's a server

Three features you approved **can't** be done by a browser alone, because browsers block cross-origin reads of other sites (CORS):
- **auto-metadata** (fetch the page's title/description/favicon/preview),
- **self-contained HTML snapshots** (fetch the page + all its resources),
- **Internet Archive saving** (cross-origin POST to archive.org).

So the app is **one local Node process** that serves the UI *and* a small API on port 4000, with all data stored **on your device**. "Same-device storage" is preserved — the server and its database live on the same machine you run the app on.

### Proposed stack

| Layer | Choice | Why |
|-------|--------|-----|
| Server | **Node.js 24 + Express** | Provided by the runtime; serves UI + API on `0.0.0.0:4000` via `npm start` |
| Storage | **SQLite (better-sqlite3)** + filesystem for snapshots/images | Single-user, same-device, no separate service; handles 500+ easily |
| UI | **React + Vite** (built, served by the server) | Rich interactions: live search, bulk select, tag-suggest, Markdown preview |
| Metadata | server fetch + **cheerio**; async (`pending`→`complete/failed`) | Non-blocking saves |
| Snapshots | **Playwright 1.61.0 / Chromium** (already installed) → self-contained HTML; PDFs passed through | Reuses the pinned browser; no second download |
| Notes | **marked + DOMPurify** | Safe Markdown rendering |
| Search | hand-written tokenizer + parser | Needed for `#tag`+boolean+phrase+literal-when-quoted rules |
| Tests | **node:test** (unit) + **Playwright** (E2E) | Cover risky logic + journeys |

### What the design artifacts pin down

- **data-model.md** — tables for bookmark, tag (unique `name_key` enforcing your single-identity rule FR-008a), bookmark_tags join, saved_search (include/exclude tags), snapshot (html/pdf), preferences singleton; plus state transitions (metadata, archive⇄, read⇄, permanent delete).
- **contracts/api.md** — every endpoint, incl. duplicate-returns-existing on POST, bulk "apply to all matching," snapshot capture/serve, archive-org, import/export.
- **contracts/search-grammar.md** — full EBNF + evaluation table + worked examples (`#js promise` = both required; `"AND"` = literal).
- **contracts/netscape-format.md** — field mapping preserving address, title, **tags, and ADD_DATE**; whole-file rejection on malformed input.

### A couple of choices worth your explicit nod

1. **Local server** (vs. a pure browser app) — required for the reasons above. Still single-user, same-device, no accounts.
2. **Tag identity is case-insensitive** — so `News` and `news` are one tag (prevents near-duplicates, matches case-insensitive search). Say if you'd rather tags be case-sensitive.
3. **Favicon + preview images cached locally** on save (best-effort) so the list works offline and survives link rot.

### 👉 At this gate

- **Approve** and I'll run `speckit-tasks` to produce the dependency-ordered task breakdown (I'll bring that back too before implementing).
- **Want changes** to the stack or any design choice? Tell me and I'll revise the plan.

I'll wait for your go-ahead.

## 📐 Plan updated — delayed-metadata safeguard added

Your three confirmations are already baked in (local helper process, case-insensitive tags so `News` = `news` per R9, local image caching per R5). The new safeguard is now explicit across the artifacts as **research decision R13**:

**The rule:** automatic details fill **only fields you haven't customized**, and can never overwrite a title/description you entered — whether you typed it while saving or edited it *while the fetch was still running*.

**How it's guaranteed (not just intended):**
- Each bookmark carries `title_user_set` / `description_user_set` flags (**data-model.md**). Supplying or editing the field — at save or later — sets its flag.
- The async metadata worker uses a **conditional write** — `UPDATE ... SET title=? WHERE id=? AND title_user_set=0` — so a fetch that finishes *after* your edit simply no-ops on that field. This closes the race you're worried about, without locking. Favicon/preview (no user-entered form) still fill normally.
- **Tested explicitly**: a unit test simulates a metadata fetch resolving *after* a user edit and asserts the user's value survives, plus an E2E check. Recorded in the Constitution Check's testability note, **quickstart.md** story 1, and the `npm test` description.

Updated files: `research.md` (R13), `data-model.md` (flags + race-safe transition + validation rule), `plan.md` (constraint + testability), `contracts/api.md` (safeguard note), `quickstart.md` (validation step + unit-test note).

## ✅ Tasks updated — "apply to all matching" now respects the whole view

The fix makes the bulk selection carry a full **view descriptor**, not just search words, so it can never reach outside what you're actually looking at.

**T039 (endpoint)** — `select.matchView` is now `{ view, q, tag, includeTags, excludeTags, sort }` (the same fields as the list endpoint). The server resolves it through the **same query + search-evaluator path as `GET /api/bookmarks`**, honoring **every** facet — view scope (normal/unread/archived), a clicked tag filter, a saved search's include/exclude tags, and the search expression — and **ignoring pagination**. So the affected set is exactly the complete current result set across all pages, and nothing outside it.

**T040 (frontend)** — "apply to all matching" sends the **exact active view descriptor**, never a bare `q`.

**Tests strengthened:**
- **T038 (E2E)** — now runs "apply to all matching" over a view that *combines* a scope (unread/archived) + clicked tag filter + saved-search include/exclude tags + search words, **spanning more than one page**, and asserts every matching item (including on later pages) changes while every non-matching bookmark (wrong scope, excluded tag, non-match) is untouched.
- **T038a (new unit test)** — verifies the server rebuilds the match set from the full descriptor identically to the list query and ignores pagination.

**Also updated:** `contracts/api.md` bulk section now specifies this descriptor and states that sending a bare `q` without the rest of the active view is a client error.

US5 now has 4 tasks (T038, T038a, T039, T040); total **63 tasks**. All other phases unchanged.
